orders.plainEnglish: You select a unit, then you right-click an order. Only the selected unit hears it. A tank and a rifle squad implement the same receive function.
orders.whyGame: Searching the whole map for the cursor every frame repeats a question the selection already answered, and it moves units you never clicked.

expansions.title: A tank
expansions.detail: The tank implements ReceiveOrder. The click does not name the tank class.

expansions.title: A squad
expansions.detail: The rifle squad uses that same function and decides what a move means for infantry.

quiz.prompt: The player right-clicks a destination. Which units should receive that order?
choices: Only the units whose Selected flag is set
Every unit currently on the map
Only units inside the fog reveal radius
The neutral camp that happens to be nearest
quiz.why: Selection is the gate.

quiz.prompt: The order excerpt branches on Selected and then calls ProcessEvent on ReceiveOrder. What does that call do?
choices: It runs the selected unit's own order function
It subtracts the sample supply cost
It marks a map cell as visible
It adds ten to the match score
quiz.why: ReceiveOrder is the unit's response.

quiz.prompt: A tank is selected and the player issues a move. Which node comes next?
choices: A fresh search of every actor for the cursor
A fog reveal that also lights the path
A medal award treating the move as a result
quiz.why: The click reaches the selected unit.

quiz.prompt: You move the cursor search onto Tick so orders feel instant. What starts walking that nobody selected?
choices: Every idle frame repeats a query, and units you never selected start walking
The mapping context forgets the right-click binding
Medals can no longer be named in data
quiz.why: The selection already knows who is listening.

quiz.prompt: A rifle squad and a tank are both on the field, and only the squad is selected. Who walks?
choices: The squad, because it is the one with Selected set
Both units, since they share one receive function
The tank, because vehicles outrank infantry
The neutral camp, because it is always listening
quiz.why: Sharing the function does not skip the flag.

quiz.prompt: An order click should move every unit on the map.
quiz.why: Unselected units do not hear the click.

quiz.prompt: What is IA_Order in this lesson?
choices: The right-click action that carries the order
quiz.why: The action is the click. The unit decides the meaning.

quiz.prompt: Art adds a new engineer unit. What must that unit implement so the existing click works?
choices: A private cursor trace on its own tick
A cast from the order graph to the engineer class
A fog write that lights the engineer by existing
quiz.why: The click never lists classes.

quiz.prompt: Which line is the order gate, not the fog write?
choices: The branch on Selected before ReceiveOrder
Visible = true after a reveal hit
quiz.why: Selected decides who hears the click.

quiz.prompt: The player clicks empty ground with nobody selected. What should happen?
quiz.why: No selected unit means no receiver.

economy.plainEnglish: Supplies are a stock you spend on purpose. A build order calls a spend event. The server subtracts the cost. The cost itself lives in a data row, not as a typed 25 in the graph.
economy.whyGame: A client that subtracts on its own spends a private stock, and the other machines still show the old total.

expansions.title: A barracks
expansions.detail: The barracks row names its cost. The graph reads the row.

expansions.title: A turret
expansions.detail: The turret has a different cost in data. It does not need a second subtract literal.

expansions.title: A broke player
expansions.detail: If the stock cannot cover the row, the spend does not happen.

quiz.prompt: A build order should spend supplies. What kind of event is that spend?
choices: A custom event the build calls once
A subtract on every frame while the building exists
quiz.why: Spend is intentional, not a tick.

quiz.prompt: The excerpt assigns Supplies = (Supplies - 25.f) inside HasAuthority. What is 25 standing in for?
choices: A sample cost that a data row should own
The only legal price for every building
quiz.why: The number is a placeholder.

quiz.prompt: The player orders a barracks and the stock can cover it. Which write comes next?
choices: The authority subtract of that row's cost
A client-side subtract so the number drops immediately
A fog bit on the building plot
Ten points added to the match score
quiz.why: The server spends the stock.

quiz.prompt: Each client subtracts 25 outside the authority check. What do the machines disagree about?
choices: Every machine spends a private stock and the totals diverge
quiz.why: One stock, written by the authority.

quiz.prompt: A barracks costs 80 and a turret costs 40. Where do those two numbers live?
choices: As two literals in the spend graph
In the medal asset by accident
quiz.why: The row names the cost.

quiz.prompt: A client may subtract supplies locally so the stock feels instant.
quiz.why: The private subtract will not match the host.

quiz.prompt: The stock is 20 and the row costs 25. What should the spend event do?
choices: Drive the stock negative and build anyway
Award a medal for the attempt
quiz.why: You cannot spend what you do not have.

quiz.prompt: Which line is the supply write?
choices: Visible = true on a reveal hit
GoingRight = true on a camp path
quiz.why: That assignment is the spend.

quiz.prompt: An order to build never calls the spend event. What does the player get?
choices: A building and the same stock they started with
quiz.why: The order has to call the spend.

quiz.prompt: Why is Tick the wrong place to drain supplies?
choices: The stock would fall while nobody is building
The authority check is illegal on a custom event
quiz.why: Spend happens when a build asks.

fog.plainEnglish: Fog is what this team can see. A short timer calls Reveal. A hit marks that cell visible. A wall blocks the look. Orders do not paint the map.
fog.whyGame: Letting a client set Visible cheats the map, and saving the bool shows camps that have already walked away.

expansions.title: A wall
expansions.detail: The trace stops. The cell beyond stays hidden.

expansions.title: A spectator
expansions.detail: Visibility is a team fact, not a widget each spectator owns.

expansions.title: After load
expansions.detail: The timer recomputes vision from positions. Do not restore the old bits.

quiz.prompt: What does the fog bool mean?
choices: This team can see that cell
A widget on one spectator's screen
quiz.why: Visible is a team fact.

quiz.prompt: Reveal assigns Visible = true when the trace hits. When does that line run?
choices: Only on a hit from the reveal timer
Whenever a camp takes a step
quiz.why: The hit is the condition.

quiz.prompt: Begin Play runs for fog. Which node should it start?
choices: A looping Reveal timer at 0.25 seconds
quiz.why: The excerpt starts that timer.

quiz.prompt: An order click sets Visible along the path. What lights up that the team never saw?
choices: Commanding a unit lights map the team has not actually seen
quiz.why: Orders must not paint fog.

quiz.prompt: A wall stands between the team and a camp. What does Reveal do?
choices: It stops on the wall and leaves the camp hidden
It marks the camp visible anyway
It orders the camp to move
quiz.why: The wall blocks the channel.

quiz.prompt: A client may set Visible true to update its own map.
quiz.why: That is a cheat. Gate the write.

quiz.prompt: The sample reveal has no authority check. What do you add before a networked match?
choices: A gate so only the authority writes Visible
A second timer at one second
A medal for every revealed cell
quiz.why: The sample is local. The match is not.

quiz.prompt: Which interval does the real Reveal timer use?
choices: The same one-second step as a camp
quiz.why: Begin Play starts 0.25.

quiz.prompt: Why is Visible not a widget each spectator owns?
choices: The team shares one fact about the map
Spectators are the only ones who should cheat fog
The camp graph is the one that writes it
quiz.why: One team, one vision.

quiz.prompt: You save Visible and load it after the camp has walked. What does the player see?
choices: A camp drawn where it no longer stands
The correct camp, because the bit follows the actor
quiz.why: Recompute vision after load. Do not restore the bit.

patrol.plainEnglish: A neutral camp walks a route nobody ordered. Begin Play starts that walk on a one-second timer. Fog decides whether you draw the camp. The camp does not light the map by walking.
patrol.whyGame: Moving the camp from Tick keeps it walking through a pause and spends a path query you already scheduled.

expansions.title: The way back
expansions.detail: The return path is empty in the sample. The camp never walks home until you fill it.

expansions.title: Drawing
expansions.detail: The client's Visible bit decides if the camp is drawn.

expansions.title: Orders
expansions.detail: The player did not select this camp. It is not waiting for a click.

quiz.prompt: Who ordered the neutral camp to walk?
choices: Nobody. Begin Play started its route timer
quiz.why: A camp is not a selected unit.

quiz.prompt: The camp path sets GoingRight = true. What did that line decide?
choices: The camp is on the outward leg
The team can see the camp
The camp just earned a medal
quiz.why: GoingRight is direction, not vision.

quiz.prompt: The camp should step about once a second. Which node does that?
choices: AdvancePatrol on the timer Begin Play started
quiz.why: The route timer owns the step.

quiz.prompt: The camp graph writes Visible as it walks. What does that walk paint on the map?
choices: Walking lights the map even when the team cannot see
quiz.why: Fog writes vision. The camp only walks.

quiz.prompt: The return path has no points. What does the camp do at the end of the route?
choices: It stops, because the walk back was never authored
quiz.why: The B path is unfinished.

quiz.prompt: A neutral camp should set Visible true on each step.
quiz.why: Vision belongs to Reveal.

quiz.prompt: The match pauses while a Tick step is moving the camp. What keeps happening?
choices: The camp keeps walking unless that step is gated
The camp is drawn through fog
quiz.why: A timer you own can pause. A raw step is easy to leave running.

quiz.prompt: The client's fog bit is false for this cell. What should the client draw?
quiz.why: Visible decides the draw.

quiz.prompt: Which line is the camp direction, not a player order?
choices: GoingRight = true on the camp path
quiz.why: The camp walks without a click.

quiz.prompt: You start a new route timer inside AdvancePatrol. What does the camp do?
choices: It speeds up as timers pile up
quiz.why: Begin Play already started the timer.

scoring.plainEnglish: A medal is a result the server records. A kill or an objective calls AwardMedal. The point value lives on the medal's data, not as a typed 10.
scoring.whyGame: A client that awards its own medal inflates a board the host never granted.

expansions.title: A kill
expansions.detail: The kill calls AwardMedal on the server.

expansions.title: An objective
expansions.detail: The objective uses the same event with its own data value.

expansions.title: The board
expansions.detail: The board shows the host's score, not a local guess.

quiz.prompt: A player captures an objective. What should record the result?
quiz.why: A medal is a result, not an order.

quiz.prompt: The excerpt assigns Score = (Score + 10.f) inside HasAuthority. What is 10?
choices: A sample value the medal data should name
The required score of every medal
The supply cost of a barracks
quiz.why: Ten is a stand-in.

quiz.prompt: The server has accepted a kill. Which write comes next?
choices: The authority add of that medal's value
A client add so the popup appears first
quiz.why: The host grants the points.

quiz.prompt: A client adds 10 outside the authority check. What does the board show?
choices: A local number the host never granted
The same score on every machine
quiz.why: The inflate never replicates as truth.

quiz.prompt: Two medals are worth 5 and 25. Where is that difference stored?
quiz.why: Data names the value, the way a row names a cost.

quiz.prompt: Giving an order should award a medal.
quiz.why: An order is not a result.

quiz.prompt: Where does the score assignment belong?
choices: On the client that saw the kill
quiz.why: The repair nests it there.

quiz.prompt: Which line is the medal write?
choices: The fog bit set after a hit
The camp facing along its outward leg
quiz.why: Score is the board.

quiz.prompt: The kill popup plays on a machine that has not heard the server score. What is that popup showing?
choices: A guess, until the authority value arrives
quiz.why: The host number is the board.

quiz.prompt: Why does AwardMedal take the value from data instead of adding 10 for everything?
choices: A kill and an objective are not worth the same points
Data assets cannot be read on the server
quiz.why: The asset names the medal.

save.plainEnglish: The match save stores supplies, score, each camp's direction, and orders that are still running. It does not store fog. After load, the reveal timer looks again.
save.whyGame: A saved visibility bit draws a camp that has already walked somewhere else.

expansions.title: Orders in flight
expansions.detail: A move that had not finished is part of the match.

expansions.title: Camps
expansions.detail: Store GoingRight so the camp continues the leg it was on.

expansions.title: When
expansions.detail: Load a finished struct at Begin Play. Do not write the slot from Tick.

quiz.prompt: Which set belongs in the match save?
choices: Supplies, score, camp direction, and orders still running
quiz.why: Save results the timer cannot rebuild.

quiz.prompt: The sample assigns SlotValue = 1.f on Begin Play. What replaces that stand-in?
quiz.why: 1 is the sample shape.

quiz.prompt: A finished struct is on disk. Which event loads it?
quiz.why: Load when the match starts.

quiz.prompt: Tick writes the slot every frame. What half-finished state gets stored?
choices: You store half-finished spends and half-finished orders
quiz.why: Write when something finishes.

quiz.prompt: You pack Visible so the map looks right immediately. What is stale?
choices: Any cell a camp has walked out of since the save
quiz.why: The timer recomputes vision from positions.

quiz.prompt: The match save should include the fog bits.
quiz.why: Reveal rebuilds them.

quiz.prompt: A camp was walking back when the player saved. What must the struct remember?
quiz.why: GoingRight is the leg.

quiz.prompt: An order was halfway to its point. Why is that order in the slot?
choices: The unit should keep executing it after load
Orders are the same thing as fog
The score is derived from open orders
The supply cost is recomputed from the click
quiz.why: In-flight orders are match state.

quiz.prompt: After load, what rebuilds the map the team can see?
choices: The reveal timer, from where units now stand
The camp step, by writing Visible
quiz.why: Look again. Do not restore the bits.

quiz.prompt: Which line is the sample save shape you replace?
quiz.why: That assignment is the stand-in.

strategy-beginner-e2: Searching the level every frame finds the cursor more honestly
Fog should decide which unit receives the click
The supply stock should gate ReceiveOrder
strategy-beginner-e4: Each client should spend so the number drops before the host answers
The fog timer is a fine place to subtract the cost
A medal award should be what spends supplies
strategy-beginner-e8: Writing Visible every frame is fresher than a quarter-second look
The camp step should be the reveal interval
Right-click should paint the cells it crosses
strategy-beginner-e13: The client who saw the kill should add the points
Reveal should add the score when a unit is visible
The order click should be the award
strategy-beginner-e15: Tick is the honest place to snapshot a live match
The right-click should be the load
strategy-beginner-e18: Every unit should walk toward the cursor
Visible should decide who receives the order
The camp direction should gate the click

exam.prompt: Tick moves every strategy unit toward the cursor. What should have gated the order?
exam.why: Only the selection hears the click.

exam.prompt: A tank and a rifle squad share ReceiveOrder. What still differs?
choices: Which of them has Selected set
Which of them owns the medal asset
Which of them stores the fog timer
exam.why: The function is shared. The flag is not.

exam.prompt: Unselected units should ignore a right-click.
Which call spends supplies for a build?
choices: The spend event, on the authority
A neutral camp taking one route step
exam.why: The build calls the spend once.

exam.prompt: The graph subtracts 25 for a barracks and a turret. What did the author skip?
choices: The data row that should name each cost

exam.prompt: The host has 100 supplies and a client has already subtracted 25 locally. What does a second client still show?
choices: Seventy-five, as if every client shared that private subtract
A wiped stock, as if a mismatch cleared it
exam.why: The private spend is not the stock.

exam.prompt: A barracks and a turret should share one typed cost in the graph.
exam.why: Each row names its own cost.

exam.prompt: What interval does Reveal use?
A right-click paints Visible along the drag. Which system was misused?
choices: Orders, which are not allowed to write fog

exam.prompt: A wall blocks the team from a camp. Which assignment must not run?
choices: Visible = true for the camp's cell

exam.prompt: Visible is one widget per spectator.
The camp reaches the end of an empty return path. What is missing?
choices: A Selected flag on the camp
exam.why: The B path was never authored.

exam.prompt: Fog's bit is false and the camp graph is correct. What does the client draw?
choices: The camp, because patrol ignores fog

exam.prompt: Which line is the camp, not the player?
choices: GoingRight = true on a path Begin Play started

exam.prompt: A camp step should mark its cell visible.
exam.why: Walking must not light the map.

exam.prompt: A kill and a finished objective need points. What do they both call?
choices: Painting what the team can see

exam.prompt: The board shows 40 on the client and 30 on the host. Where was the extra 10 added?
choices: In the save struct's fog bits

exam.prompt: Where should a medal's point value live?
choices: As the literal 10 for every award

exam.prompt: Loading a match should restore every Visible bit.
Which event loads a finished match struct?
You are choosing what to pack. Which item do you leave out?
A camp was on the return leg. The load starts it outward. What field was dropped?
The player builds a turret, reveals a wall, and never clicks a unit. Which writes are allowed?
choices: The authority supply subtract and the reveal hit
A cursor move of every unit and a client-side medal
A camp write of Visible and a tick snapshot
A local supply subtract and a saved fog bit
exam.why: Spend and reveal are the two events that fired.

exam.prompt: Tick is a valid place to write the match slot.
Which pair is a result versus an order?
choices: The supply row versus the fog bit
Begin Play versus the save struct
exam.why: A medal records. An order commands.

exam.prompt: The stock cannot cover the row. What still must not happen?
choices: The camp taking its next step

exam.prompt: A spectator widget stores its own Visible flags. What can that player do?
choices: Mark unseen cells as seen on their own screen
Grant a medal the host records
exam.why: Vision has to be a team fact.

exam.prompt: Begin Play starts both a fog timer and a camp timer. Which one writes Visible?
choices: Both timers, which would keep the map bright
Neither timer, if the click were what paints fog

exam.prompt: In-flight orders belong in the match struct.
exam.why: The unit should keep executing them.

exam.prompt: You need the line that gates a click, the line that spends, and the line that awards. Which trio is that?
choices: The Selected branch, the authority supply subtract, and the authority score add
What the team can see, plus camp direction, plus the sample slot
Three copies of the same tick search
A client subtract, a client score add, and a saved fog bit

exam.prompt: After load the map shows a camp in a cell the team can no longer see. What was restored?
A new unit type arrives from art. What does the order graph not need?
choices: A cast to that new class

exam.prompt: The pause menu is up and camps are still sliding. Which step is running?
choices: A per-frame move that was never paused
exam.why: The route timer can be paused. A tick slide often is not.

exam.prompt: The sample cost 25 and the sample medal 10 should both move into data.
exam.why: Rows and assets name those numbers.
